title: My Top Scholar Husband Climbed a Higher Branch, So I Married a Powerful Minister
author: Chen Huan
synopsis:
When Xie Zigui lacked silver, Wen Mingyue was his salvation, his predestined good match. When Xie Zigui lacked power, Wen Mingyue was his stumbling block.

In order to climb up to a concubine-born daughter of a Marquis's estate as a shortcut, Xie Zigui disregarded the grace of saving his life and abandoned his childhood sweetheart.

Yet, upon seeing the woman in his second brother's arms, so familiar, he could not help but redden his eyes.

chapters.title: Mistaken for a Mistress
chapters.content:
"My lady, don't listen to the nonsense people outside are spouting. What kind of character does our master-husband have? Others might not know, but how could you not?" Peilan stood under the eaves, hands on her hips, speaking not so much to Wen Mingyue as to let the people outside hear.

The master had only the young lady as his child, and after the master passed away, the Wen family's estate naturally all fell upon Wen Mingyue.

Though she had no brothers to prop her up, heaven had not been unkind to the young lady.

When the master-husband was eight years old, he was taken in by the Wen family. Back then, he was skinny and tiny, unable to even feed himself while begging along the streets, yet he still had to take care of his sickly mother.

Wen's father pitied him for showing such filial piety at a young age and thus saved their mother and son.

The Wen family was the savior of Xie Zigui and his mother.

Yet after all these years of living day and night together, who in the entire household did not praise Xie Zigui for valuing affection and righteousness?

On the day of Wen's father's funeral, it was Xie Zigui who wore sackcloth and filial piety to see him off, and furthermore swore a solemn oath in front of everyone that he would regard Mingyue more importantly than his own life in this lifetime.

The master-husband was willing to study; how much silver had been poured into him all these years?

Now that he had placed high in the imperial examinations as the Top Scholar, it was naturally time for the young lady to enjoy blessings.

Because this new Top Scholar was busy with official duties, the master-husband had arranged for a manservant to come ahead and report, so they could meet in Pingcheng, pay respects to the Xie family ancestors, and then head to the capital together.

As for the Wen family's shops, the master-husband had also said they did not need to be abandoned; Wen Mingyue would forever be the proprietor of the Wen family. Once she accompanied Xie Zigui to the capital and got familiar with it, if Wen Mingyue wanted to stay in the capital she could stay, and if she didn't want to, she could return to the Wen family, and by then Xie Zigui would run back and forth.

Such thoughtfulness.

After traveling through wind and dust, they finally arrived in Pingcheng. No sooner had they settled down than a woman came knocking, whom they initially thought was a neighboring relative, only to find out she was a gossipy busybody.

Right off the bat, she asked whose mistress the young lady was so they could be companions in the future and figure out ways together to force the household to acknowledge them as concubines.

She even claimed that the ones in the front courtyard had successfully entered the mansion just days ago.

These words made Peilan so angry she could barely breathe. Her young lady was a proper, legitimate first wife; if not for Xie Zigui's upcoming imperial examinations, the government registry would right now state that Xie Zigui was a matrilocal son-in-law raised by the Wen family!

Wen Mingyue sat on the recliner, truly feeling somewhat weary from the journey these past few days. She rubbed the space between her eyebrows and helplessly curved the corners of her mouth, "Since you know she was talking nonsense and she has already been sent away, don't go getting yourself angry over it."

When she went on a long trip, her several shops were all managed by reliable people, and she didn't have many people following by her side. It was probably because others looked down on her shabby appearance that they mistook her identity.

While they were talking, the maidservant had already tidied up the bed, and she helped Wen Mingyue up to rest on the bed.

The light green skirt hem swayed slowly and then stopped. "If the master-husband comes back, instruct him..." Wen Mingyue paused abruptly, "to wake me up."

After months apart, there were naturally many words of longing to be spoken.

She originally thought they could meet upon entering the city, but she didn't expect Xie Zigui to be detained by the prefect, saying he would return later.

Meeting him now made her somewhat nervous.

Those unpleasant words could wait to be dealt with another day.

Wen Mingyue was not as hot-headed as Peilan; she carefully pondered everything in her mind. Just now, another detail occurred to her: this street was clean and spacious, yet the gate of this courtyard lacked any brightness, and most importantly, the surroundings were far too quiet; there wasn't even the sound of peddlers crying their wares.

This place most likely had a story to it.

She had originally thought of asking Xie Zigui to rent a courtyard elsewhere, figuring he was a newcomer who didn't know the local ropes, but on second thought, they wouldn't be staying many days before heading to the capital anyway, so enduring it for a few days would suffice.

chapters.title: Husband and Wife Become Brother and Sister
chapters.content:
Leaning against the bed, her brows slowly relaxed.

After a journey of rushing all the way, a solid, grounded feeling was indeed the most comforting.

Yet as soon as they relaxed, they furrowed again. "Peilan, if anyone else comes to the door talking nonsense, send them straight to the magistrate's office."

She had thought it better to avoid trouble where possible, but Xie Zigui was the new Top Scholar, and local officials were bound to pay visits and entertain wherever he went.

If such an incident blew up, there would inevitably be people harboring the mentality of watching a good show.

Xie Zigui had no clan backing, and his wife was a merchant's daughter. If she tolerated it to the point of acquiring a reputation, there would be no telling how much trouble would follow later.

Even if it made a big fuss, at worst Xie Zigui would just say, "My wife is unmannered," passing down a reputation that Wen Mingyue was overbearing and intolerant.

As the head housekeeper of the Wen family, could Wen Mingyue not even handle being an official's wife?

Upon hearing this, Peilan immediately broke into a smile, as if more than half of her anger had dissipated. She didn't know the ins and outs of these matters; as long as her own mistress wasn't bullied, that was all that mattered.

Wearied by the continuous travel, Wen Mingyue was exceedingly tired and slept straight until dark.

Opening her eyes in a daze, she instantly sobered up. "Zigui." The two names held in her heart slipped right past her lips.

"Young lady." Hearing the commotion, Peilan hurriedly pushed the door open, brightened the candlewick, and nimbly rolled up the bed curtains. "The master-husband has not yet returned. This servant has already sent someone to wait outside."

At this hour, even official business should have been finished.

Ever since he first arrived and sent someone to relay a message, there had been no further movement, making even Peilan somewhat flustered.

"As the sky grows dark, take torches and keep watch outside." While speaking, Wen Mingyue had already gotten up, looking outside with worry etched across her face.

Seeing how secluded this place was during the day, the roads would surely be difficult to navigate at night.

Knowing that Wen Mingyue was worried about Xie Zigui, Peilan swallowed back the words of persuasion she had wanted to say.

They waited another hour. The food in the pot was heated over and over again, forget about the rest, but if that fish wasn't eaten soon, it might become toxic. In the end, Peilan couldn't hold back and advised Wen Mingyue not to wait anymore.

Yet just as Wen Mingyue shook her head, she heard a commotion outside, and the voices of the servants gradually grew clear.

"The master-husband is back." It was as if a gloomy sky had suddenly cleared up; even Peilan's voice carried undisguised joy.

Wen Mingyue hurried to her feet, and just as she reached the doorway, Xie Zigui strode over.

Having not seen each other for months, he seemed to have lost a lot of weight; there was no flesh on his cheekbones, and there were dark circles under his eyes.

"How is it you've grown so thin?"

The two spoke at the same time, their brows furrowed in identical frowns, before suddenly looking at each other and smiling.

Peilan directed the servants to quickly serve the food so she could withdraw as fast as possible.

Presumably, this couple had plenty of words to share.

"What are you keeping stuffed in there, all bulging?" Words of longing failed to escape her lips, leaving only an ordinary inquiry.

For someone so thin, the clothing over his chest was conspicuously bulged out.

Xie Zigui, who was a head taller than Wen Mingyue, bent slightly, looked left and right before carefully taking out the item from his bosom.

"Knowing you love to eat this, how could I not prepare it?"

What he pulled out was Wen Mingyue's favorite sesame flatbread.

The grease from it had soaked through a large patch of Xie Zigui's clothes.

"Aren't you afraid of people laughing at you!" Wen Mingyue scolded playfully, giving his shoulder a light punch. After all, he was the new Top Scholar; if outsiders saw this, it might provoke idle gossip.

Xie Zigui waved his hand indifferently, and just like usual, before the meal, he first wiped a clean towel for Wen Mingyue to wash her hands. "It's not for anyone else, what do I have to fear?"

When he handed it to Wen Mingyue, his eyes were full of smiles.

Those eyes seemed capable of speaking, hooking Wen Mingyue's face into a blush. Not daring to look at him, she hurriedly sat down.

"What do you think of this Pingcheng prefect?" Her face felt too hot, so Wen Mingyue wanted to quickly shift her attention.

After sitting down, Xie Zigui very naturally began picking fish bones for Wen Mingyue. If not for the Wen family's rescue, he might have long ago fallen to the streets and suffered every hardship. Coupled with the fact that Wen Mingyue was not one to put on airs, most of the time when the two were alone, servants were not needed to wait upon them. Thus, looking after Wen Mingyue fell entirely on Xie Zigui.

Even now, with their circumstances vastly different from before, this remained unchanged.

Xie Zigui gave a cold snort, "In the few days I've been in Pingcheng, I've found that the rich have endless silks and satins, while ordinary commoners struggle even to secure three meals a day."

To put it bluntly, it was either extreme wealth or extreme poverty.

Hearing this, Wen Mingyue's brows knitted together involuntarily.

"Not only that, he even openly hit me up for congratulatory silver." He put it nicely, calling it sharing in the good fortune of the new Top Scholar.

This was openly showing utter disregard for the law.

Wen Mingyue pressed her lips together tighter and tighter. Truly a scourge to the local commoners.

Mentioning this matter, Xie Zigui put down his chopsticks and solemnly took Wen Mingyue's hand. "They say a mighty dragon cannot crush a local serpent. Since we are passing through this place, we have no choice but to rein in our sharpness. Fearing he might harbor malicious intentions, I only told him you are my distant cousin."

Just being a relative, naturally, there was no need to attract attention.

If he had said they were husband and wife, Xie Zigui feared he might offend the officials of Pingcheng and cause Wen Mingyue to suffer.

"You and I share one heart as husband and wife, naturally we don't fear those ghosts and demons!" Wen Mingyue shook her head, disagreeing. Xie Zigui was, after all, the new Top Scholar; if something really happened to him in Pingcheng, it could directly alarm the Emperor.

Xie Zigui sighed softly, "I dare not gamble."

Wen Mingyue was his life; he could even die, but Wen Mingyue could not come to any harm.

He rubbed the palm of Wen Mingyue's hand. "I only blame myself for being incompetent. If I had the ability to be enfeoffed as a marquis or become a prime minister, I would never let you suffer this humiliation."

He wished he could announce to the entire world how fortunate he was to have such a virtuous wife.

"Your hand." Wen Mingyue, however, noticed the roughness of his palm.

His were hands meant for holding a writing brush; they had never done rough labor.

She abruptly turned over Xie Zigui's palm, and an unsightly, winding scar on his left hand reflected into Wen Mingyue's eyes. Her hands trembled, her eyes filled with tears, "Th-this, what happened here?"

Xie Zigui gave a dry laugh and awkwardly pulled his hand back, "It's just something I got from a fall while traveling."

"Just where does one fall to end up looking like this?" Wen Mingyue suddenly raised her voice. She had thought that being the new Top Scholar meant being cloaked in glory, but reality proved otherwise.

Xie Zigui let out a long sigh, "Let's not talk about it."

The commoners do not contend with officials, and minor officials do not contend with major ones.

Xie Zigui smoothed down Wen Mingyue's hair. "Being an official is different from doing business; you cannot afford a single misstep."

In the past, it was Wen Mingyue who protected him; in the future, it would be him protecting Wen Mingyue.

Wen Mingyue gently shook her head. Being an official was sometimes similar to doing business, both required careful calculation and deliberate scrutiny.

However, before she could voice it, a servant hurried over, whispered a few words into Xie Zigui's ear, and stepped back.

Xie Zigui's expression shifted slightly, and he immediately stood up. "the Prefect has summoned me for an errand. I must leave first and will return tomorrow."

He hurried away in such haste that the wind stirred up by his coattails blew a pair of chopsticks off the table, blocking the path where Wen Mingyue wanted to step forward.

chapters.title: A Courtesan?
chapters.content:
Wen Mingyue had just bent down to pick up her chopsticks, but when she looked back up, Xie Zigui was already gone.

Hurried footsteps blended into the evening shadows.

Peilan, who had just finished bustling about, was leaning against the side chatting idly with the servants downstairs. Seeing that Xie Zigui’s expression was off, she quickly tossed aside the melon seeds in her hand. "My lady, what's wrong with the master again?"

Resting her hand on the armrest, Wen Mingyue slowly sat down.

"Pingcheng is not peaceful." To think they could be so daring and lawless to this extent.

She tapped her fingers gently on the tabletop, then slowly raised her head. "Since Pingcheng is not peaceful, then grain must be in short supply."

It wasn't that grain didn't exist; it was simply that it was monopolized by those with power and influence.

Scholars who became officials overnight naturally looked down from on high, but merchants like them had their own means of survival in this world.

The Wen family's primary business was grain trading. Finding a way to navigate this situation would not be a difficult task.

As the head of the Wen family, Wen Mingyue had her own strengths to contend with men for a share of the world.

She was not the kind of delicate flower who would hide behind a man just because her husband had achieved success.

Whatever Xie Zigui lacked the time to consider, Wen Mingyue naturally could figure out for him.

She hadn't managed to eat more than a few bites of her meal. Anxious to write a letter back to Zhaozhou City, Wen Mingyue remained awake while Xie Zigui had already left.

At an hour when everyone should have been resting, the lights in Wen Mingyue's room blazed bright.

She was preparing the letter so Peilan could send it out the moment the city gates opened wide the next day.

Grinding the ink stick beside her, Peilan already understood the whole situation. "My lady, couldn't we use their own strength against them?"

Wen Mingyue paused the brush in her hand and shook her head slightly. "For the officials in Pingcheng to dare act so audaciously, there must be someone backing them in the capital."

If they rashly tried to use outside force, she feared they might accidentally hit the wrong target and lose more than they gained.

Peilan pressed her lips together and remained silent. Her mistress was always thoroughly thoughtful.

With her mistress firmly holding down the inner courtyard, her master, who aspired to become a Marquis or a Prime Minister, could rest easy.

If her mistress were a man, it was hard to say whose the top scholar's seat would be.

Early the next morning, Peilan personally set out to leave the city.

The time had been carefully calculated, but the sun climbed high into the sky and still Peilan had not returned. Wen Mingyue began to feel restless. She sent someone out to make inquiries, and, unable to quell her worry, stood by the doorway to wait in person.

"Tsk, tsk." The door next door opened, and a woman dressed in bright red with her hair coiled up leaned against the doorframe at a slant. Even though she was dressed decorously, her posture exuded a heavy air of the pleasure quarters.

Wen Mingyue glanced at her sideways and paid her no mind.

Unperturbed, the woman even swayed her hips and strolled slowly toward Wen Mingyue.

As she drew closer, the pungent perfume wafting from her made Wen Mingyue frown.

"Such a cold and aloof look. If she were placed in a brothel, she'd certainly fetch a pretty penny." The woman looked Wen Mingyue up and down, her very first words betraying her origins.

"Say that again!" The maid behind Wen Mingyue immediately flared up. "Do you know who my mistress is?"

"Hold your tongue!" Wen Mingyue cut the maid off. Though she disagreed with Xie Zigui's plans, she would not undermine him nor presumptuously put on airs as the top scholar's wife.

Besides, the Wen family came from a mercantile background; what harsh words hadn't she heard before?

Moreover, having sat as the head of the Wen family for so long, she possessed her own natural dignity.

She gave the woman a faint, sweeping glance, causing the latter to let out a dry, awkward laugh. "Why so fierce? I didn't mention your names, I was just talking to myself."

With that, the woman flicked her handkerchief and retreated, swaying her waist.

"If we were in Zhaozhou City, I'd make her pay for that!" The maid spat in disgust. Ever since yesterday, she hadn't seen a single person around here she could look at without frowning.

One and all, where did they gather such a bunch of disreputable characters?

"Watch your words and behavior!" Wen Mingyue issued a warning. She had nothing to fear for herself; she was only worried about Xie Zigui.

People were made of flesh and blood. Over the years, Xie Zigui had always put her first. Wen Mingyue had long since stopped caring about any so-called "life-saving grace"she simply considered things purely for the sake of her husband.

A husband and wife had to advance hand in hand if they were to accompany each other to old age.

For Xie Zigui's sake, she could swallow this anger.

Fortunately, Peilan returned. Even though her forehead was slick with sweat, she had at least made it back safely.

Furthermore, the guards who escorted Peilan were completely unharmed.

"My lady, this servant..." Peilan looked left and right as she spoke, then hurried Wen Mingyue inside the room to talk.

Even then, she carefully checked behind them and shut the door tightly before speaking.

"This servant ran into someone from the Prefect's residence who was out purchasing supplies." Peilan lowered her voice. On her way back, she had smelled freshly cooked sesame flatbreads and stopped, remembering that Wen Mingyue liked this exact snack. Since it was still early, she thought she'd bring some back.

While waiting for the flatbreads, she overheard some people chatting nearby.

They were complaining about how they had eaten too much rich food and meat these past few days and fancied some flatbread for a change.

Then they started gossiping about how big an official the new top scholar was.

Sensing something was amiss, Peilan bought a few extra flatbreads and lingered to listen a bit longer.

That was how she learned the two maids were procurement servants from the Prefect's residence. These days, they were walking on eggshells serving the new top scholar, having hosted countless banquets and invited numerous guests of honor to accompany him.

The Wen family was also a wealthy household, and Peilan was a trusted senior maid in front of the family head, what grand scenes hadn't she witnessed? Even so, hearing about that level of extravagance had shocked her greatly.

Anyone who didn't know better would have thought the Prefect was sucking up to Xie Zigui.

Listening to this, Wen Mingyue also sensed something was wrong. "When are they holding these banquets?"

She had people stationed outside the Prefect's residence to gather information. Yesterday's encounter had been too rushed, leaving no time to talk properly, but today she needed to ask in detail.

It was also to warn Xie Zigui that he must take action now; he could not let the Prefect tarnish his reputation.

"Wait." Wen Mingyue pondered for a moment. "Pack up our valuables."

If the situation turned sour, they would pack up and leave early.

Ancestor worship was, after all, not as important as saving one's life. As long as the green hills remain, there’s no need to worry about firewood.

Calming herself, Peilan hurried off to busy herself with the task.

Though Peilan had brought back two batches of sesame flatbreads, Wen Mingyue didn't have the heart to take a single bite of either.

However, Xie Zigui returned quite early this time.

He came back right after noon. Wearing the same new robe and the same oil stains, the only difference was that Wen Mingyue kept her guard up. She picked up the flatbreads to test them: they were warm, yet noticeably softer than the ones Peilan had brought back.

One batch had just come out of the pan, while the other had clearly been reheated a second time.

He had merely passed the imperial examination to become the top scholar, why had he learned to lie to her?

"I found an excuse to slip out, and that's when I spotted our people hiding in the shadows." Xie Zigui naturally recognized the people by Wen Mingyue's side. "I figured you were looking for me, but since I happened to pass this flatbread shop, I couldn't very well return empty-handed."

"You and I are husband and wife, a single entity. Is there truly nothing you can be honest about with me?" Wen Mingyue abruptly cut through his casually fabricated lie.

Wen Mingyue was no fool.

Xie Zigui froze for a moment, then lowered his gaze.

chapters.title: Caught Red-Handed
chapters.content:
Seeing Xie Zigui remain silent, Wen Mingyue impatiently rubbed the space between her brows.

"Aren't you planning to explain how you got that wound?" Wen Mingyue was reluctant to direct suspicion toward her own family.

If there was something to be said, it should be laid out openly and honestly.

Xie Zigui did not speak. Feeling blindly along the edge of the cabinet, he inched his way over until he finally found a chair and slowly sat down.

He opened his palm, revealing a gruesome scar that was glaringly offensive to the eye.

Wen Mingyue was in no rush either, simply waiting quietly in place.

After a long while, Xie Zigui suddenly let out a light, bitter laugh. "It's fortunate this wound is on my left hand. If it were on my right, my life would be ruined."

Though his left hand looked fine from a distance, it couldn't lift anything heavy at all.

If his right hand had been injured, he would never be able to hold a brush again.

When he left, he was full of grand aspirations; when he returned, he was utterly wretched.

Clearly, he had passed as the top scholar, yet he couldn't feel the slightest bit of joy because he knew this road ahead was still very long.

"I saw him. My father." Xie Zigui's voice slowly turned ice-cold, a trace of murderous intent even flashing through his eyes.

Yet immediately after, he could no longer conceal the bitterness at the corners of his mouth.

He had watched his own father so meticulously protect that woman; watched his father fail to recognize him even when their eyes met; watched his father scold him simply because he lingered a few moments too long.

His wound had indeed happened in a place where he shouldn't have fallen, but it wasn't an accidental slip; he had been pushed.

He hated it. How could he not hate?

Back when he was reduced to a state of destitution in Zhaozhou City, the story was that he had suffered a calamity and been separated from his father. But from subsequent remarks, the Wen family had long since guessed where that man had gone.

Father Wen only had one daughter, Wen Mingyue, so naturally he had to scrutinize the match carefully.

It was true that Xie Zigui was filial, but he was far more filial to his mother. Having suffered the bitterness inflicted by a scumbag father, he would never become a man like that.

Wen Mingyue let out a long sigh and pulled Xie Zigui into an embrace. She opened her mouth several times to speak, but each time felt like the wrong moment.

In truth, she had assumed that Xie Zigui's talk of ancestor worship wasn't just about returning home in glory, but also about holding his head high.

"I have no choice but to wallow in the mire with them," Xie Zigui used the most humiliating term possible to describe himself.

Yet he had no other option. He wanted to maintain his lofty integrity, but he lacked the capital to do so.

People only cared whether you stood high; no one cared how you climbed up.

As the new top scholar, he would one day undoubtedly stand at the head of all officials.

He slowly raised his head. "The suffering my mother endured, I will make sure you never taste."

When that time came, he would surely secure an official noble title for Wen Mingyue, allowing her to enjoy the utmost honor bestowed by the imperial court.

This temporary concealment was for the sake of a better future.

Therefore, he had to act close to the officials down here.

Only then did Wen Mingyue let out a breath of relief. Merchants weren't overly obsessed with right and wrong; she merely stopped worrying about Xie Zigui.

She pulled a chair over and sat down close to him. "Still, you must be on guard against that man."

If they were truly wallowing in the mire together, what was the need for such grand, superficial spectacles?

"I know what I'm doing." Xie Zigui patted the back of Wen Mingyue's hand. "I know what I'm about. I shouldn't have dragged you into this, but my yearning overpowered my reason. Even if we had to maintain the facade of a brother-sister relationship, I had to be with you."

Wen Mingyue cast a coquettish, reproachful glance at him. "Listen to you, spouting such nonsense."

The warmth between them had finally been restored, but unexpectedly, a servant rushed in and whispered a few words to Xie Zigui.

Xie Zigui stood up once again. "I have matters to attend to. I'll explain everything in detail when I get back."

"I..." Wen Mingyue rose as well, but before the words "I'll go with you" could leave her lips, Xie Zigui had already hurried away once more.

Even after laying everything bare between them, there was still no real closure.

Feeling uneasy, Wen Mingyue quickened her pace and followed him outside.

"Brother Zigui!" The moment Xie Zigui stepped out the door, a figure dressed in male attire came skipping toward him.

As she smiled, the corners of her mouth curved up, revealing dimples on her cheeks that made her look all the more vivacious and charming.

No matter the dark colors or the oversized robe, they couldn't conceal her identity as a young woman.

"Why are you here?" Xie Zigui hurried forward to welcome her.

"Isn't it a surprise?" The young woman lifted the hem of her skirt, her steps quickening even more the moment she caught sight of Xie Zigui.

"Naturally." Xie Zigui nodded repeatedly, though he anxiously looked back to ensure the courtyard gate remained tightly shut per his instructions, only then breathing a sigh of relief.

"You must be exhausted traveling all this way. I'll take you somewhere to rest." Xie Zigui exchanged a glance with his men, signaling them to quickly bring the carriage around.

This person wasn't from the Wen family; she was someone he had bought in the capital after placing as the top scholar.

"How could I be tired? Mother sent a bunch of people along, and knowing I like to play around, she even wrote a formal calling card specifically for me." She had marched straight to the Prefect's residence with that card. If not for that, how else could she have tracked him down so quickly?

"So this is your younger sister here in Pingcheng?" Chattering away, she suddenly looked past Xie Zigui toward the courtyard.

Xie Zigui stiffly turned his head to see that the tightly shut courtyard gate had been opened, and Wen Mingyue was standing inside, gazing at them from afar.

"Yes. My sister doesn't like meeting people. You go wait in the carriage; I'll be right there." Xie Zigui swallowed hard, instinctively letting go of the hand he had been holding.

The young woman looked from Wen Mingyue to Xie Zigui. "Alright. Make sure you put in a good word for me in front of your sister, don't let her blame me."

Xie Zigui murmured an assent and motioned to his men to quickly escort this "great deity" away.

The moment she was away from his side, he hurried over to Wen Mingyue in a trot.

He reached out to take Wen Mingyue's hand, but she dodged his touch. "Is this what you meant by an urgent matter?"

Urgent to go see some young lady?

Xie Zigui waved his hands and hurriedly signaled for the door to be closed. "Listen to my explanation."

"Go ahead, I'm listening." Though a vague guess had formed in Wen Mingyue's mind, and stormy waves were churning in her heart, she maintained an extraordinary outward calm.

A calm so profound it left Xie Zigui entirely at a loss for how to respond.

"I..." Xie Zigui took a deep breath. "Mingyue, in this lifetime I recognize only you as my wife. But now that I am an official in the imperial court, there are some situations your background simply cannot handle."

The wives of those high-ranking officials in the capital, which of them didn't come from illustrious families? A merchant's daughter wasn't even fit to be a concubine.

Xie Zigui only wanted her lineage secured.

"Rest assured, she is utterly foolish; she believes whatever I coax her into believing. I will be able to enter that household very soon, but the family will still only recognize you as the mistress of the house. She is no match for you at all." Ten fools like that couldn't compare to a single Wen Mingyue.

"What is her background?" Wen Mingyue interrupted his rambling, repetitive guarantees.

If swearing oaths actually worked, what need was there for laws?

"The concubine-born daughter of a Marquis's estate." Xie Zigui spoke in a very soft voice, carefully observing Wen Mingyue's reaction with every syllable he uttered.

Wen Mingyue nodded. "A Marquis's estate... Ah, well, that's certainly worth your while to cast away a wife who shared the hardships of poverty."

chapters.title: Wife Becomes Concubine
chapters.content:
The Wen family’s social standing naturally could not compare to that of a marquis’s estate.

Since childhood, people had always said that Xie Zigui’s eyes and brows looked full of spiritual brilliance, and he was bound to amount to something in the future.

And indeed, he had! The newly minted top scholar had become the prized son-in-law of a marquis’s estate; just this alone set him apart from ordinary men.

For some reason, Wen Mingyue felt a slight dryness in her eyes. To think she had painstakingly devised plans for Xie Zigui’s future, only to find out she was merely indulging in unrequited affection.

"All these years, you should know my temperament. I am not someone who clings stubbornly. All you had to do was say 'no,' and I wouldn't have tangled with you!" Why lower herself to chase him across mountains and rivers just to become a laughingstock?

"Mingyue!" Xie Zigui suddenly raised his voice. "She is merely a tool for my revenge! How could she ever be compared to you?"

In this lifetime, Xie Zigui loved only Wen Mingyue. In this life, the next, and even lifetimes after that, that would never change.

Xie Zigui had also weighed the options: the marquis’s estate was in decline, run by an aunt by marriage; the legitimate daughter was a fool, and this illegitimate daughter was utterly simple-minded.

As for the younger brother, he was far too rash to uphold the prestige of the marquis’s estate.

To the marquis’s estate, he himself was an ingrate who bit the hand that fed him.

But so what? Once he climbed to a position of supreme power, who would care how he got there?

At worst, he could burn a few more stacks of joss paper for them every Qingming Festival.

"But I am not willing!" Wen Mingyue frowned impatiently. These were all Xie Zigui’s own wishful thoughts, not her original intention.

As the head of the Wen family, she had been living a carefree life. Why should she lower herself to compromise and wait for some distant future?

"You said husband and wife are one." Knowing Wen Mingyue’s temper, Xie Zigui anxiously reached out to grab her hand. Seeing her step back, he persistently pursued her. "We have depended on each other for survival. Just consider this as helping me get my revenge, won't you? If you don't wish to see her, you can often go out."

So, just as he had said in his letter, he would not interfere with Wen Mingyue’s freedom.

Before Wen Mingyue could refuse, Xie Zigui dropped straight to his knees before her. He had his own proud bones, but in front of Wen Mingyue, he was willing to grovel at her feet.

His eyes were red-rimmed, looking up at Wen Mingyue as pitifully as when they had first met.

Peilan had originally wanted to step in for Wen Mingyue, but his sudden kneeling left her speechless. With a wave of her hand, she simply left the two of them alone.

"Yet, you are another woman's husband." Wen Mingyue slowly lowered her head, casting aside her calm composure to speak purely from the perspective of an ordinary woman.

"I won't touch her!" Xie Zigui promised eagerly.

His body and soul belonged only to Wen Mingyue; they would never be sullied.

As for that woman outside, it was nothing more than play-acting.

"Don't treat everyone else like fools!" Wen Mingyue laughed out of anger. Was he trying to coax her like a little girl? Won't touch her? You might not touch her for a day, two days, a month, or two months, but how on earth could you fool someone over the long haul of months and years?

Seeing Xie Zigui behave this way, the background of the father he was sucking up to certainly wasn't low. How could the justice he sought be easily obtained?

"She is a fool." For instance, just now, the atmosphere between himself and Wen Mingyue was obviously wrong, yet she simply couldn't see it.

She was naturally missing a screw compared to others; she was far too easy to hoodwink.

"She... how is she innocent?" Without having suffered his hardships, Wen Mingyue could not judge his decisions. But how could she sit back and reap the rewards with a clear conscience?

"She fell into the water that day and I saved her. The debt of a life saved must be repaid," Xie Zigui immediately countered. He hadn't begged for this marriage; she had offered it willingly.

He had even once asked her jokingly if she was willing to give everything for him, and she had said yes. So what else was he reluctant to part with?

Wen Mingyue slowly closed her eyes. "You should leave first. I need to think, and so do you."

After all, this concerned a lifelong matter. Whether to agree or not required careful thought.

"Mingyue, what do you need me to do so you will believe me?" Seeing Wen Mingyue’s previously softened attitude revert to a cold, keep-others-at-a-distance calm, Xie Zigui grew even more anxious.

If he could, he would even tear open his own chest to let Wen Mingyue check if her name was carved upon his heart.

Wen Mingyue’s expression suddenly turned icy. "You have harbored your hatred for ten years, yet you force me to accept it in a single breath. How cruel is that?"

Saying she needed to think it over was already her being polite and sparing his face; did he really have to force her to spell things out bluntly?

Chastised, Xie Zigui lowered his head. "Yes... I was too impatient."

There was still a long time ahead; he would eventually make Wen Mingyue see his true intentions.

With an "mn," Wen Mingyue turned and walked away, not bothering to ask where Xie Zigui was headed.

"My lady, what is to be done?" Back inside the room, Peilan sat before Wen Mingyue, looking at her mistress with heartache.

No matter how eloquently Xie Zigui spoke, it didn't change the fact that he was reducing her mistress from a wife to a concubine.

Whether Xie Zigui had any entanglements with that marquis's estate lady back in the capital, Peilan didn't care; she only felt distressed for her mistress, suffering such an injustice for no good reason.

Wen Mingyue sat blankly for a moment before letting out a soft sigh. "I will stay here for three days. After three days, we leave."

Actually, there was nothing really to think about.

It was simply that he found her social standing too low and had climbed up to a higher branch. She would simply grant him his wish.

Life was only a few short decades. Her father often said that no one was worth wasting her youth on. As the sole daughter of the Wen family, her father had never demanded how filial she needed to be when she grew up, only that she must never wrong herself for the sake of others.

Raised under her father’s tender protection, if she were to willingly lower herself and act servile, the first person she would fail is her father.

She believed Xie Zigui also had grand ambitions, and the people by his side were merely accessories.

In the end, the one standing beside him would simply be the most suitable person.

Yet, having come full of joyous anticipation, she had been caught so utterly off-guard. She needed time to adjust her mood. Three days; she figured three days would be enough.

She had just been about to have her luggage packed, planning for the two of them to leave together. Now that saved the trouble; she would only pack her own things.

Peilan nodded heavily. "My lady is wise."

Like the bright moon hanging high in the sky, untainted by the dust of the mortal world.

Speaking of leaving, Peilan suddenly remembered, "Tomorrow, I’ll have the people below purchase a few more sesame seed cakes."

Wen Mingyue liked them; she had to eat her fill of them.

Wen Mingyue chuckled, amused. "No matter how much you like something, if you had to make a living selling it, you wouldn't like it anymore."

As soon as she said it, she paused. Things were like that, and people ought to be the same.

Once you let go, you find ease. There was no need to worry about Xie Zigui’s future anymore. The exhaustion of many days suddenly washed over her, and now she just wanted to sleep in utter darkness where no one could disturb her.

Yet the wind rose during the night, blowing open the window beside the couch, and Wen Mingyue woke with a shudder.

Hearing the movement, Peilan hurried in. "Why did it blow open? It was my carelessness; I forgot to latch it."

Noticing the exhaustion plastered across Wen Mingyue’s face, Peilan didn't want to disturb her further and hurriedly tidied up before retreating, never expecting such a mishap.

chapters.title: Knowing He’s Taken, Yet Stepping In
chapters.content:
Peilan’s movements were swift, bang, closing the window with a speed as if she feared Wen Mingyue might catch sight of some filthy thing.

That person standing in the corridor, Wen Mingyue had actually seen him, but both sides tacitly avoided mentioning it.

What was there to talk about? Talk about how deep his affection supposedly was?

And what use was deep affection? Wen Mingyue couldn't live on deep affection alone.

Since she had made up her mind, seeing him was the same as not seeing him.

Letting him feel, at least, that he had no regrets.

Because his deep affection could not compel her to bow her head.

She rolled over, closed her eyes, and went back to sleep.

Perhaps because she had slept her fill, Wen Mingyue felt extraordinarily refreshed the next morning. It would have been even more perfect if an uninvited guest hadn't shown up.

When Wen Jiashu sent over a calling card, Wen Mingyue had no intention of seeing her. However, all sorts of shadowy gossips were craning their necks outside, prying into the drama at her doorstep.

Perhaps out of a sudden soft-heartedness, Wen Mingyue had them let her in.

It was just that Peilan’s news arrived a step ahead. "My lady, the situation doesn't look good."

The subordinates reported that the carriage they had prepared had been inspected early this morning.

The excuse given was that the city was unsafe, and everyone's travel permits had to be taken to the yamen for re-stamping.

Since it was just a matter of getting a fresh seal, Peilan hadn't thought much of it and went over early. Up until her turn, things had gone smoothly, but the moment the yamen officials saw her documents, they confiscated them outright. They were polite enough, saying that Zhaozhou City was far from Pingcheng, and perhaps some checkpoint along the way had missed stamping them; once they finished checking, they would naturally return the items to Peilan.

Peilan gnashed her teeth in anger, but being on someone else's turf, even a fierce dragon had to curl up. She could only bite her tongue and agree.

With their belongings confiscated, they wouldn't be able to leave the city anytime soon. Even if they managed to sneak out, they wouldn't be able to enter anywhere else.

"It must be him!" Xie Zigui had stood outside her door half the night yesterday, presumably to put on a display of deep affection. Although no one paid him any mind, they hadn't chased him away either.

He had probably figured out their intention to leave.

Truly a changed man; they hadn't even done anything yet, and he was already flashing his official authority right in front of them.

The fable of the farmer and the snake was truly playing out before their eyes.

Her complaints came to an abrupt halt as Wen Jiashu walked in.

Today, she had changed into women's attire, wearing pink and tender clothes that made her look all the more dainty and charming.

"Little Sister," she took a step forward. "I ought not to be older than you in status, but I must follow Brother Zigui in addressing you this way."

Wen Mingyue did not offer her a seat, but Wen Jiashu was not one to stand on ceremony; she sat down directly on Wen Mingyue’s left.

"What a coincidence, my surname is Wen too." Only, this surname "Wen" was worlds apart.

One was the high-and-mighty lady of a marquis’s estate, while the other was merely a merchant’s daughter fallen into the dust.

Seeing the unexplained arrogance blooming on Wen Jiashu’s face, Wen Mingyue let out a sudden chuckle.

The simple-minded girl Xie Zigui kept going on about didn't look like this at all to her. "So, Wen Lady, did you come today to talk to me about fate?"

Wen Jiashu smiled and shook her head. "Naturally not."

She leaned forward slightly. "I know your relationship with Brother Zigui, but the man I have set my eyes on can only be mine."

"Oh? Are you here to fight me for him?" Wen Mingyue raised an eyebrow slightly. "Wen Lady, I won't comment on your conduct, but if you want to fight for a man, you should go find the man himself, not come looking for me."

Wen Mingyue didn't care to critique the upbringing of the marquis’s estate; she was just speaking strictly based on the facts.

Wen Jiashu blinked. "I know, but his heart has you in it, so I naturally need to excise it."

She had her own plans, such as securing her official status.

At least in the capital, the position of Madame Xie would be hers.

With just a few sweet words, Xie Zigui had believed she was easy to manipulate; his tactical retreats had only allowed her to push her advantage further.

Seeing Wen Jiashu’s look of absolute certainty, Wen Mingyue found Xie Zigui’s confidence all the more ridiculous.

"I hear Wen Lady is an illegitimate daughter?" Wen Mingyue looked at her with a half-smile. "Though I once heard someone say that the maid of a great household is superior to the daughter of a humble family. I suppose I shouldn't measure you, miss, by those vulgar standards of legitimate versus illegitimate birth."

In the business world, what mattered most was psychological warfare.

When Wen Mingyue insulted someone, she never used a single dirty word; slow-witted people wouldn't even catch the deep irony beneath her words.

Unfortunately for Wen Jiashu, she was no fool. Wen Mingyue was mocking her for fighting over men like a concubine-born daughter, calling her inferior even to a household maid of a reputable family. Such words were scathing indeed.

"Audacious!" It was the first time Wen Jiashu had ever been scolded like this, and she slammed her hand fiercely onto the table.

"You're the audacious one!" Peilan refused to yield either; was she just going to let someone ride roughshod over them?

Wen Mingyue raised a hand in a gentle gesture, signaling Peilan to step back. "Since Wen Lady is from the capital, I suppose you eat the emperor's grain. But unless Wen Lady mentions it, please forgive my unobservant eyes; I am unaware of your official title."

This knife thrust hit home viciously.

Before the emperor, a married noblewoman could receive a imperial title, and an unmarried maiden could be granted a noble rank like Princess or Commandery Princess. Since she claimed to be a lady of a marquis’s estate, surely she must at least be a Commandery Princess?

Wen Mingyue leisurely sipped her tea, her expression brimming with absolute certainty: Wen Jiashu was a complete nobody!

Wen Jiashu bit her lip hard. She had truly underestimated this merchant's daughter.

"Mingyue, Jiashu." As the room fell quiet, Xie Zigui’s rushed footsteps shattered the oppressive silence.

Wen Jiashu hurriedly stood up, hastily putting on her naive and cute smile once more. "Brother Zigui, you're back?"

Stepping into the room, Xie Zigui first threw an anxious look toward Wen Mingyue. Seeing her expression seemed normal, he then turned to Wen Jiashu. "Why are you here?"

Because Wen Mingyue was present, Xie Zigui didn't dare act too intimate, making his tone dry and stiff.

Wen Jiashu, however, failed to notice, hooking her finger into the corner of Xie Zigui’s sleeve. "Naturally, I came to deliver the invitation to Little Sister."

The wife of the Pingcheng prefect was exceptionally warm and insisted on hosting a welcome banquet for Wen Jiashu. The invitation had been sent to the top scholar's fiancée, and naturally, it included Wen Mingyue, her nominal "younger sister."

"It's just that Little Sister seems to lack enthusiasm, and I was hoping you could persuade her." Wen Jiashu let out a long sigh. "No matter how quiet Little Sister's temperament is, she'll have to get used to it eventually. When we return to the capital together, these social events are unavoidable."

"I know." Xie Zigui anxiously cut Wen Jiashu off, terrified that Wen Mingyue would fly into a rage and spill the raw truth.

Sensing something off in Xie Zigui’s tone, Wen Jiashu instantly felt her eyes turn red. "D-did I meddle too much?"

Xie Zigui frowned instinctively, but ultimately softened his tone. "I know you mean well, but these things take time."

Seeing Xie Zigui return to his usual attitude, Wen Jiashu beamed with her customary bright smile. "It was just me being impatient. I won't do it next time."

She then pulled a gold-stamped invitation from her bosom. "Then you talk it over nicely with Little Sister."

With that, she curved her eyes into crescents as she looked at Wen Mingyue. "It doesn't matter whether you go or not; I've got you covered anyway."

chapters.title: Persuading Her to Become a Concubine
chapters.content:
A newly minted top scholar and the face of a marquis’s estate, a mere prefect below them could not afford to deny them.

Having said this, she raised an eyebrow and glanced at Xie Zigui, as if waiting for him to praise her.

Xie Zigui gave a perfunctory nod. "Yes, yes, yes, our Jiaoshu is the most capable. Since we are attending a banquet, go and prepare first, and see if there are any ready-made clothing styles you like."

It didn't have to be the best, just something novel.

Wen Jiaoshu nodded heavily. "I'll go right now and buy a few sets for Younger Sister as well." With such a wonderful idea, Wen Jiaoshu looked like a little girl who had received a piece of candy, skipping as she walked out.

"Look at her silly appearance." Xie Zigui withdrew his gaze and commented mockingly to Wen Mingyue.

Silly? If Xie Zigui had seen the calculating look that filled the eyes of that marquis's estate young lady just moments ago, how could he possibly utter such words?

Hasty hunters almost always appeared in the form of prey.

"Since she's so silly, why don't you coax her into becoming a concubine?" Suddenly, Wen Mingyue wanted to push him, forcing him to tear off his mask of deep affection.

"If, if it were just her alone, of course that would be fine, but after all, there is the marquis's estate." Xie Zigui was confident on this point; Wen Jiaoshu was very easy to coax and would do whatever he told her to do.

It wouldn't be long before he took control of the marquis's estate, and then he could raise Wen Mingyue to the position of a legitimate wife.

Wen Mingyue gently shook her head. "We don't need the marquis's estate. Just you and me, even with just you and me, we can reach high positions."

She believed she was no less capable than the young lady of the marquis's estate.

"But Mingyue, I can't wait." That scene encountered in the capital was a hatred that he could not shake off.

When they reached the capital, they might run into him frequently; without sufficient backing, how could he hold his head high in front of him?

To tell him that even without him as a father, she could still live very well.

"So what are you dragging me along for, then?" Wen Mingyue's gaze suddenly turned sharp. "Are you holding me back and not letting me leave because you're afraid I'll go back and ruin your good plans?"

They were a proper husband and wife who had walked through the yamen doors; if he wanted to marry the daughter of a marquis, he inevitably had to make proper arrangements in Zhaozhou City.

She had said she wouldn't throw a wrench in his works, and that they would part on good terms.

Xie Zigui truly did not need to use such despicable methods.

"Mingyue, I said it before, I want you." Why was there so much suspicion between them? He had played tricks, but wasn't it also because he was afraid Wen Mingyue would leave him?

For so many years, Wen Mingyue had always been by his side; only with her near him could his heart be at ease.

Did he tell lies so often that he even believed them himself?

If she were truly that important, why would he watch with his own eyes as she suffered grievances?

When she first lived here, Wen Mingyue had thought Xie Zigui was being played by someone else, but now it seemed the arrangements were made just right.

What kind of brother and sister relationship was so unspeakable that upon arrival, she was made to stay in a corner? Probably a paramour.

Then, settling her in a place specifically designated for kept mistresses, wasn't that just right?

Xie Zigui knew the local customs of Pingcheng; he couldn't possibly be unaware of the implications here.

If even the past was a lie, then this person in front of her forced her to be on guard.

"I understand. You should hurry and leave, lest your fiancée becomes suspicious?" Wen Mingyue said indifferently.

Yet Xie Zigui wore a look of pleasant surprise. "Does that mean you agree?"

Xie Zigui suddenly picked Wen Mingyue up in his arms. "I knew it, I knew you still had me in your heart. For my sake, you would certainly be willing."

Even to become a lesser wife.

Wen Mingyue hurriedly patted Xie Zigui to make him put her down. "Since she's a silly girl, aren't you afraid I'll bully her?"

"Bully her if you want. She ran away to become a concubine of her own accord; in my heart, she isn't as important as a single strand of your hair." Xie Zigui spoke with utter indifference. "I originally planned to slowly discuss this with you in Pingcheng, but now that she has arrived, it caught me off guard. Otherwise, I wouldn't want you to suffer even a fraction of a grievance."

Look at that, Wen Mingyue smiled self-deprecatingly; he was indeed guarding against her.

"Didn't Miss Wen come to deliver an invitation? I naturally must attend the banquet." Wen Mingyue softened her tone, sounding as usual.

"This." Xie Zigui hesitated. The main thing was that the prefect's side would certainly center around Wen Jiaoshu. If Wen Mingyue went there in an unfamiliar place, she would probably be ostracized.

"You've been jolted all the way along this journey." Meaning, he didn't agree.

Wen Mingyue impatiently turned a thumb ring on her finger, the kind mostly worn by men, belonging exclusively to the head of a household. "I'll have to adapt eventually. Could it be that you actually plan to 'hide a golden house'?"

Truly making her a kept mistress who could never see the light of day?

"Look at you, saying such things. I put you first in everything; I'm just afraid you'll feel uncomfortable. If you're fine with it, how could I be unwilling?" Xie Zigui moved a bit closer. "I'm sorry, hiding it from you was my fault. Aside from this matter, I won't keep anything from you in the future."

They were husband and wife sharing and facing everything together.

"Mm." Wen Mingyue nodded, leaned back in her chair, and then slowly closed her eyes.

Clearly, she had no desire to speak with Xie Zigui.

Xie Zigui slowly raised his head and affectionately stroked Wen Mingyue's hair. "Do you know that you are my life?"

Therefore, in this lifetime, no matter what, he would never let go.

He would selfishly keep Wen Mingyue by his side forever.

Aside from this matter, he would find ways to compensate Wen Mingyue for the rest of his life, giving her things that other women would envy.

Xie Zigui stayed here with Wen Mingyue for a while. Seeing that she had no intention of speaking further, he gave a light sigh. "Think it over carefully. Our days ahead are still long."

Once she figured it out, good days would surely come.

Wen Mingyue's eyelashes trembled slightly, but she never raised her eyes.

Waiting until the footsteps by her ear faded away, Wen Mingyue finally opened her eyes, straightened her body, and looked outside.

"Mistress, what should we do now?" Peilan grew more flustered the more she pondered.

Yet Wen Mingyue remained calm on the surface. With her parents gone, managing the Wen family as household head for all these years had long since trained her to remain calm in the face of adversity.

"I suppose it's time to properly meet that young lady from the marquis's estate." Wen Mingyue had originally intended to lay her cards on the table and force him to look into his own heart.

However, when Wen Mingyue realized that perhaps all past events were merely his calculations of pros and cons, if everything was a fake, then exposing it all wouldn't be meeting each other with sincerity, but flying into a rage out of humiliation.

Human hearts; they were the most complex and also the most cold-hearted.

"Send word back. Let everyone in the Wen family perk up their spirits." Since she couldn't leave Pingcheng, she would find a way to get the message out and let the Wen family protect themselves first.

Although the weather should have been warm, Wen Mingyue felt a chill all over her body.

Fortunately, Wen Mingyue had slept extremely well last night, so she had the spirit to attend the banquet now.

When the time came, Xie Zigui didn't bother with Wen Jiaoshu; instead, he came to greet Wen Mingyue in person.

After all, the two of them were nominal brother and sister and couldn't get too close, one sat in a carriage while the other rode a horse.

The carriage was stuffy, so Wen Mingyue lifted the curtain. As they passed the doorways of various courtyards, she saw heads poking out.

chapters.title: Superiority Made Clear
chapters.content:
As well as pairs of envious eyes.

Envious of Wen Mingyue for flying up to a high branch.

A legally wed wife becoming a role model for a kept mistress, how was that not laughable?

Fortunately, she could pretend not to see it; and fortunately, both her parents were gone. Otherwise, seeing their daughter in this state, they would probably be envious.

The carriage moved slowly, and along the way, they did see quite a few places.

True to Xie Zigui's words, some places were truly impoverished while others were luxurious.

Finally, they arrived outside the prefect's residence. Two stone lions stood majestically at the front; the main gate looked somewhat aged, but that only added a sense of solemn dignity.

"Top Scholar, you've finally arrived." Before Wen Mingyue had even stood steady after getting down from the carriage, someone came out from the estate to welcome them.

Xie Zigui glanced at Wen Mingyue, but after all, it wouldn't do to appear too intimate, so he simply gave a light nod and a "Mn." His upright figure carried the impressive bearing of the current top scholar.

"This must be the Eldest Miss. Madam has already prepared tea and is waiting for you." The steward was a shrewd fellow; seeing Xie Zigui's gaze drifting toward Wen Mingyue, he immediately chimed in.

Yet his words gave one much food for thought, especially the title "Eldest Miss"how very meaningful.

It both demonstrated an awareness of her status and avoided awkwardness.

Wen Mingyue gave a slight nod, then lifted her skirt with one hand and followed behind Xie Zigui.

Even though she felt the assessing gazes of others, she still looked straight ahead.

In the eyes of the world, Wen Mingyue was naturally an accessory to the top scholar; yet in her posture, Wen Mingyue was high and mighty, even giving people the illusory, disjointed impression that she was herself and the top scholar was himself.

Unlike the unadorned main gate, entering the courtyard brought a sense of towering oppression.

Wen Mingyue had never been to the imperial palace, but she imagined the palace could scarcely exceed the grandeur she felt within the prefect's residence.

The passing maids all kept their heads down and walked with hurried steps, the four characters "strict hierarchy" carved directly onto everyone's face.

"Mistress, please come this way." Walking past the outer courtyard into the inner courtyard, a matronly servant naturally stepped forward to guide Wen Mingyue.

Xie Zigui, being a male outsider, naturally had to stop. After pondering repeatedly, he still pulled on Wen Mingyue's sleeve. "Don't be nervous."

Wen Mingyue seamlessly stepped away, and a trace of a smile appeared at the corners of her lips.

"The prefect's madam is naturally kind-hearted. As a junior, having the fortune to be favored by Madam is a rare blessing indeed. My heart will only be filled with joy; I won't be nervous." With that, Wen Mingyue nodded to the matron.

She didn't miss the surprise in the matron's eyes.

Indeed, merchant daughters were naturally considered beneath them, but other people aside, how could Xie Zigui not know that she, as the head of the Wen family, likewise had to meet with officials?

Naturally, meeting madams happened less often.

Xie Zigui also reacted, offering an awkward laugh. "Of course."

Wen Mingyue was exceptional; previously, circumstances had forced it, but now he wanted to suppress her and make her look up to him. Therefore, at times, he probably deliberately ignored her glorious past.

Wen Mingyue followed the matron inside, while Xie Zigui remained waiting outside.

It wasn't until someone on the side coughed, reminding Xie Zigui repeatedly, that he finally snapped out of it and remembered the prefect was still waiting for him.

Wen Mingyue placed her hand on the back of Peilan's hand, and out of the corner of her eye, she saw Peilan holding her back remarkably straight.

Especially compared to those people in the prefect's residence who only knew how to lower their heads and bow, she looked particularly distinctive.

"Mistress, please wait a moment." Outside the door of the room, the matron did not lead Wen Mingyue directly in, but went inside to report first.

Wen Mingyue smiled faintly and in silence, letting the matron play those little games.

Fortunately, the delay wasn't long. Soon, the beaded curtain was lifted, and Wen Mingyue was led inside.

Unexpectedly, the prefect's madam did not possess the nobility she had imagined; at least in appearance, she wasn't particularly outstanding, and her height was not notable either.

Her slender eyes revealed shrewdness.

As merchants, they naturally had to be well-traveled, and might even know a bit of physiognomy, understanding how to speak differently to different people.

"This commoner greets Madam." Wen Mingyue released Peilan's hand and offered a graceful bow.

"Someone from Top Scholar Xie's household shouldn't stand on ceremony; please rise quickly." The other party made a vague lifting gesture with her hand, then looked with a full smile toward Wen Jiaoshu at the side. "I was just wondering if you two would come together."

These words were truly full of meaning.

Wen Jiaoshu immediately smiled coquettishly. "I have an impatient temperament and can't stay quiet, so I came out to walk around first. I hope Madam won't find me noisy."

Listening to it, there didn't seem to be anything wrong with it either.

Wen Mingyue picked up the teacup beside her and took a gentle sip. "The tea by Madam's side is more fragrant than that in any other estate."

The prefect's madam narrowed her eyes. "Oh, then I'm truly curious, whose estates are those?"

It sounded like a joke, but the delivery was aggressive.

Clearly, she was being somewhat petty, trying to make things difficult for Wen Mingyue.

Yet Wen Mingyue remained calm and collected. "This commoner is ashamed; there aren't many others. The best tea I ever had was at the Prefectural Administrator's estate. The fragrance of that tea lingered on the teeth and lips, leaving a memory I still can't forget. Having tasted Madam's tea today, I finally know what true perfection is."

Upon hearing this, the prefect's madam hastily waved her hand. "How could my tea compare to the Prefectural Administrator's? Miss, please don't tease me like this."

Even if no one else was listening, such treasonous words could not be spoken.

Wen Mingyue did not press her advantage, instead changing the subject. "Madam governs her household with clarity and order, and her etiquette is thorough. No matter where you are, you are an outstanding figure. In the future, when My Lord receives a promotion, you will naturally be a model for the region."

Talking about coming together, wasn't that humiliating someone?

What relation did Wen Mingyue have with Wen Jiaoshu? Not to mention that Wen Jiaoshu hadn't even married in yet; even if she had married in, she wasn't necessarily a concubine of her household, why on earth should she come with her?

Furthermore, it was her estate that had sent out the invitation asking them to come.

Now that they had come, was there any logic to blocking someone outside the door?

Was this implicitly trying to suck up to Wen Jiaoshu? It's just that the method was a bit clumsy.

"Wen Younger Sister, please say no more. How can we wildly discuss matters of the imperial court? Fortunately, there are no outsiders around; if there were, wouldn't it make people laugh at us for being frivolous?" Wen Jiaoshu immediately took over the conversation, naturally trying to suppress Wen Mingyue.

Wen Mingyue's gaze remained fixed on the prefect's madam's face. "This commoner is foolish, and merely thought Madam was much more than this."

Setting aside status, purely in terms of means, trying to ingratiate oneself with Wen Jiaoshu like this was altogether too shallow.

The prefect's madam understood Wen Jiaoshu's meaning, and a respect that hadn't been there before crept into her brows and eyes. "Miss, don't be nervous. It's just us women sitting together for a chat, talking nonsense just to liven things up."

She then raised a hand to signal the servants below: since Wen Mingyue loved this tea, keep the cups refilled diligently.

As for Wen Jiaoshu, she had originally intended to hold a high position, yet Wen Mingyue refused to give her even a straight glance.

And yet, you couldn't find a single fault with her behavior.

They granted Wen Jiaoshu honor because she was the top scholar's fiancée and a lady of the marquis's estate; but if you looked closely, these didn't properly belong to her own status yet. If she wanted to act high and mighty, she should wait until she truly became a high-ranking court official's wife.

chapters.title: A Happy Cooperation
chapters.content:
Now she was merely a secondary daughter of a marque's estate. To put it bluntly, she naturally had even less standing.

Seeing the prefect's wife step forward, Wen Mingyue naturally stopped while she was ahead, simply replying, "Great sounds are rare, great forms are without shape."

Then, she exchanged a knowing smile with the prefect's wife.

The spotlight belonging to the marque's daughter was thus overshadowed by Wen Mingyue.

The prefect's wife could not help but sigh inwardly; this concubine's daughter was truly extraordinary. Had it not been for the disparity in their status, the marque's daughter might not have been a match for her.

Wen Jiaoshu naturally sensed the shift in the prefect's wife's attitude and felt anxious inside. But the more anxious she grew, the more mistakes she made. "Junior sister has a glib tongue, I've seen it for myself today."

Only then did Wen Mingyue slowly set down her teacup, looking at Wen Jiaoshu with a smile that wasn't quite a smile. "If my judgment serves me right, I should be a few years older than you. I truly don't understand where this 'younger sister' business comes from?"

With that, she glanced at the prefect's wife. After all, there were only three people here, and if this "younger sister" wasn't meant for her, it must be a self-reference.

As an unmarried young lady, it surely wasn't proper to claim relation through a fiancé.

The prefect's wife understood the situation clearly, inwardly marveling at how formidable this concubine's daughter truly was. People pursued profit, and if the prefect's wife favored Wen Jiaoshu, it was only for the sake of the person standing behind her. But right now, Wen Jiaoshu's position was hardly secure; naturally, she wouldn't step forward to bail Wen Jiaoshu out and offend Wen Mingyue in the process.

Right at that moment, a subordinate hurried in to report, and the prefect's wife could only offer an awkward smile and excuse herself.

She provided good tea and hospitality simply to find an excuse to leave.

Once outsiders were gone from the vicinity, Wen Jiaoshu dropped all pretense entirely. "What? Do you really think you can compete with me?"

Even if she herself was a fool, even if everyone around them thought Wen Mingyue was more capable, so what? As long as she was a member of the marque's estate, a merchant's daughter would never be able to surpass her.

Wen Mingyue shook her head gently. She had no intention of offering explanations; the gentle are often taken advantage of. If Wen Mingyue didn't fight back, there was no telling how many people would step on her.

It wasn't for Wen Jiaoshu's sake; she simply didn't have the habit of swallowing her anger.

Right now, however, Wen Mingyue looked at Wen Jiaoshu very seriously. "Do you want me to drive a wedge between you and Xie Zigui? Do you want to possess Xie Zigui completely?"

Since there were no longer any feelings left, she addressed him by his full name.

If she hadn't kept her temper in check, she would surely have ridiculed Xie Zigui for being blind and foolish, welcoming a poisonous scorpion into his midst while mistaking her for pure and kind.

The more they quarreled like this, the further they would push Xie Zigui away.

"You are a clever young lady; you must have realized that I am not someone willing to swallow insults. I certainly will not stay by Xie Zigui's side. But commoners do not fight officials. I must ensure my own safety. Tell me how you want me to cooperate, and I will cooperate accordingly." Let alone arguing, even if it meant going to a brothel to patronize courtesans, why wouldn't it be possible?

"You merchant daughters really are utterly shameless." Wen Jiaoshu let out a disdainful, cold scoff. No wonder people always said merchants were of the lowest class; look at this woman, casually speaking of such things.

At least she herself wasn't as vulgar as this!

"Your meaning is that you won't cooperate?" Wen Mingyue suddenly raised her voice. They were supposed to be cooperating; it wasn't as if she were begging her.

Wen Jiaoshu straightened her posture. "What kind of guarantee do you want?"

How could safety be assured?

"I want a marriage certificate!" Wen Mingyue said with a firm tone. A marriage certificate endorsed by the yamen; that would be Xie Zigui's Achilles' heel.

"You can rest assured, Miss; I will not make a mockery of my Wen family's ancestral heritage. I only seek peace and stability." Wen Mingyue wouldn't engage in a destructive showdown with them; everyone had people they needed to protect.

Xie Zigui had undoubtedly already reached his tendrils into Zhaozhou City, and while she had connections with the official yamen, no connection could ever outweigh officials protecting one another.

Therefore, Wen Mingyue had appeared in this place to have a proper discussion with Wen Jiaoshu.

She could no longer trust Xie Zigui. True to her own words, as the head of the Wen family, she naturally had to use the most secure method.

Those who betray cannot be trusted again, nor will she fail to leave herself a way out.

Seeing that Wen Jiaoshu remained silent, the agonizing wait made anxiety grow, her fingers unconsciously turning her jade thumb ring.

"Since you have already grown weary of Lord Xie, I only need to wait. Why should I soil my hands with ash?" Wen Jiaoshu shifted her straightened body a bit further forward.

"Has Miss ever heard the saying, 'Drive a dog into a corner and it will inevitably bite back'?" Wen Mingyue stopped turning her thumb ring, the corners of her mouth curling up slightly.

If she couldn't secure any guarantees, she would drag everyone down into the water together.

"Fine. Give me five days. After five days, I will fetch the document and give it to you." Wen Jiaoshu stood up. "And then, I will personally select a husband for you."

She refused to believe that a soiled woman could still remain immaculate in Xie Zigui's heart.

"Then, happy cooperation." Wen Mingyue nodded in satisfaction. After all, everyone had the right to fight for their own future.

It wasn't something reserved exclusively for men.

After they reached an agreement, the prefect's wife returned. Because terms had been settled, the meal proceeded in a harmonious atmosphere, completely devoid of the previous tense, swords-drawn hostility.

Once the meal was over, the prefect's wife personally escorted the two of them out.

Xie Zigui had received word and was already waiting at the entrance early on.

Though those who suffer early in life are often clever, through years of careful observation he had learned to meticulously parse the emotional shifts in everyone's eyes. He had assumed that among aristocratic officials, Wen Mingyue, a mere merchant, would inevitably suffer.

Yet judging by the posture of the three women walking over, the prefect's wife walked closer to Wen Mingyue, suggesting she favored her more.

"Top Scholar Xie is truly considerate." The prefect's wife saw them out and made a playful remark.

Yet she didn't specify who was being considered, perhaps leaving unsaid what she truly wished to express.

"You flatter me, Madam. My foster sister has caused you trouble." Xie Zigui raised his hands in a bow, his posture humble.

The prefect's wife smiled faintly and said no more.

After bidding farewell to the prefect's wife, Wen Mingyue walked toward her carriage first. "Let's go."

Passing by Xie Zigui, she dropped those two words.

"Alright." Xie Zigui quickly agreed.

However, in full view of the public, Wen Jiaoshu grabbed Xie Zigui's sleeve, her eyes slightly red.

"Jiaoshu," Xie Zigui called out helplessly. Yet Wen Jiaoshu, usually so obedient, stubbornly refused to let go at this moment.

Wen Mingyue looked back at the entangling pair, a trace of mockery on her lips, and then quickened her pace.

"Mingyue, I'll send Jiaoshu off first. I'll come see you shortly." Xie Zigui hesitated for a moment, but ultimately chose Wen Jiaoshu.

Peilan looked back and called out in a huff, "Aren't we leaving yet?"

Who on earth was this driver waiting for anyway?

Wen Mingyue dropped the carriage curtain, refusing to look at Xie Zigui any longer.

She felt only an even deeper sense of fortune for having kept her wits about her, not falling for Xie Zigui's tricks.

Had she listened to Xie Zigui's nonsense about never wronging her, she would have ended up hurt all the more.

Five days. In five days, she could live the life she desired.

From then on, the sky was high and the road was long, may they truly never meet again.

She needed to make proper arrangements for Peilan. The Wen family's people would arrive soon, just in time to deploy them.

Wen Mingyue had long understood the truth that one should not put all their eggs in one basket.

chapters.title: Either a Filthy Disease or Pregnancy
chapters.content:
As the carriage neared the estate, Xie Zigui actually rode up on horseback to catch-up.

"Why were you walking so fast?" The carriage stopped, and Xie Zigui quickly dismounted, casually tossing the reins to a servant.

With a smile on his lips, his heart and eyes seemed entirely filled with Wen Mingyue.

"If I didn't leave, what should I have done?" Wen Mingyue looked straight ahead, her expression completely blank.

The remaining words, stay and watch you two play lovebirds? were left unsaid, and she had no intention of saying them.

Xie Zigui took a few quick steps forward. "Don't you know my true intentions? I was merely humoring that foolish girl so she would hurry back. You and I are the ones meant for the long haul."

Only by placating Wen Jiaoshu first could he be at ease to watch over Wen Mingyue.

Wen Jiaoshu was temporary; Wen Mingyue was forever.

That remark calling her "that foolish girl" was sickening to hear.

Back in her room, Wen Mingyue had Peilan bring water for her to wash her hands. She washed them over and over, feeling a persistent itch all over her skin, as if somewhere on her still carried filth.

"Still, you shouldn't constantly bicker with her. What harm is there in giving her a bit of face in public? She's simple-minded; if you humor her a little, wouldn't the days we spend together be much easier?" Seeing that Wen Mingyue's expression hadn't noticeably changed, Xie Zigui weighed his words and muttered a reminder from the side.

"What did she say to you?" Wen Mingyue paused in her hand-washing, turned her head to fix her gaze on Xie Zigui, and before he could speak, cut him off. "Did she say I made her lose face in public?"

Wen Mingyue let out a cold scoff. "What did you want me to do? Should I have sat while she stood? Should I have fed her while she ate?"

With that, Wen Mingyue irritably tossed her towel heavily into the basin, completely unbothered as the splashing water wet her clothes. "That's the posture of a concubine, not mine!"

Xie Zigui hurried forward to grab Wen Mingyue's hand. "Look at you, we were just talking, why are you getting so worked up? Don't you know my feelings? We are husband and wife; we're just putting on a show for her together."

Wen Mingyue jerked her hand away from Xie Zigui's grasp, her face chilling as she retreated into the inner room.

Xie Zigui followed closely behind step-for-step. "Stop being angry. Let the grievance be mine to bear; you truly shouldn't have been dragged into this. I'll handle her end, do whatever you want."

Listening to Xie Zigui's words, Wen Mingyue only found them grating.

He wanted to exact his revenge like a rat in the gutter, yet stubbornly dragged her down with him without ever asking if she was willing.

Just as her father had said, a true villain wasn't difficult to deal with; the truly troublesome ones were the hypocrites.

For some reason, hearing Xie Zigui ramble on like this made Wen Mingyue feel nauseous. She had originally intended to suppress the feeling, but that discomfort peaked under the barrage of Xie Zigui's words, and she couldn't help retching.

Xie Zigui's expression turned unsightly, but he still stepped forward to gently pat Wen Mingyue's back, helping her catch her breath.

Hearing the commotion, Peilan cast aside all hesitation, pushing open the door directly, flinging the window wide open, and instinctively ordering the servants outside to immediately bring in fresh tea.

Someone feeling nauseous could not stomach foul odors; since there would be a bad taste in her mouth after retching, Peilan naturally considered every detail.

Unlike Xie Zigui, who just stood there like a wooden post.

Peilan cursed Xie Zigui inwardly. For some reason, she couldn't understand why she hadn't found him this unbearable before.

Fortunately, once Wen Mingyue calmed down, Peilan swiftly brought her tea.

Wen Mingyue slowly closed her eyes, feeling utterly exhausted all over.

Xie Zigui pulled the quilt over Wen Mingyue from the side, placing a hand on her forehead, thankfully, she didn't have a fever.

Xie Zigui had spent most of the day with the prefect. Though he didn't reek of alcohol like ordinary middle-aged men, incense had been burning in the prefect's room, and the heavy sandalwood scent radiating from his cuffs when he moved made Wen Mingyue, who had just barely settled down, start dry heaving again.

Seeing this, Xie Zigui retreated a step. "What's wrong?"

Wen Mingyue shifted further inward. "Change into my favorite pear blossom scent."

Without spelling it out, her words made Xie Zigui's expression turn dark. "I'll go bathe and change my clothes right now."

Wen Mingyue closed her eyes without answering.

Xie Zigui stood nearby for a moment, let out a long sigh, and ultimately walked out.

"Why is it that my lady was perfectly fine, but came back from the prefect's estate like this?" Peilan asked, tears of worry falling.
