She had used rouge to brighten her complexion when they went out, but now, no amount of rouge could mask her pale face.

"I'm just tired. I'll feel better after sleeping for a bit." Wen Mingyue's voice was very soft, clearly lacking strength.

As for anything else, she had no heart to dwell on it now; closing her eyes, she only wished to empty her mind of everything.

When she opened her eyes again, the horizon had been dyed red by the setting sun.

After such a sleep, she felt considerably more energetic.

Peilan was keeping watch in the outer room; hearing the sound of Wen Mingyue getting up, she immediately came in to attend to her.

"Where is he?" After tidying up and drinking a cup of tea, Wen Mingyue finally asked.

At the mention of Xie Zigui, Peilan's anger flared anew. After Wen Mingyue finished vomiting, he had put on a hypocritical show of concern outside, asking everyone how her health had been lately.

Yet someone had come from outside and called Xie Zigui away with just a few words.

He had claimed he would return shortly, yet look at the hour; he still hadn't appeared.

Since Wen Mingyue and he were nominally brother and sister, he certainly wouldn't be coming over tonight.

Peilan could figure out with her toes that the person who called Xie Zigui away could only be the prefect or that marque's daughter. Xie Zigui hadn't even officially taken up his post yet; regardless of who summoned him, it was just socialization, nothing of real importance.

Peilan could only marvel at how perceptive Wen Mingyue was. If she were an ordinary woman unable to let go, she would only end up washing her face with tears day after day.

Hearing Peilan say Xie Zigui wasn't here, Wen Mingyue immediately instructed her, "Go summon a doctor right away, as fast as possible."

Seeing the urgency in Wen Mingyue's command, Peilan didn't ask questions and immediately passed down the order.

She had thought summoning a doctor would be a trivial matter, but as the sky grew darker and darker and still there was no sign of a doctor, Peilan completely lost her patience and sent someone to investigate.

The servants were innocent enough; they had gone to several medical halls, offering ample silver, paying whatever fee was demanded for a house call. Everything seemed fine at first, but the moment they mentioned where they lived, the doctors immediately reneged and even had people chase them out.

"What kind of wretched people are these?" Peilan was so angry her teeth itched. With eyes blind to status, did they think she'd default on a medical fee?

"Go on. Double the fee. If double isn't enough, triple it. If triple won't do, offer a hundred taels! I refuse to believe we can't hire a doctor!" Wen Mingyue heard it clearly from inside the room and raised her voice to issue the order.

Peilan waved her hand to signal the servants to hurry and handle it, while trying to set Wen Mingyue's mind at ease. "Why should my lady lower herself to bicker with such people?"

"I know it's not their fault." Wen Mingyue took a deep breath. Anyone living in this particular residence wasn't living a proper, upright life; the people who sent for doctors here either had a filthy, shameful disease, or were pregnant behind their master's back.

chapters.title: How Good I Am to You.
chapters.content:
If it were a filthy disease, ordinary doctors would certainly steer clear of it.

For a woman, seeking medical attention was already difficult.

If she were pregnant, that would be even more scandalous. They were merely concubines, of the lowliest status. Should the master of the house find out, how could the primary wife ever spare them?

If a fight broke out, the doctor would find himself needlessly tainted with trouble.

Mainly, everyone avoided this place. If it were minor ailments or petty illnesses, the women here actually went outside to see physicians; the only ones unable to walk out and needing someone to come here were precisely these two afflictions.

Yet, Wen Mingyue slowly raised her head. "Suddenly feeling nauseous, I am truly frightened."

She was, after all, a woman. Having taken over the Wen family’s shops, there were certainly people waiting to pounce on a household with no male heirs, so Wen Mingyue had no intention of having a child. It was just that Xie Zigui was leaving for the imperial examinations, and since they were about to be separated, Wen Mingyue had acted on impulse for a moment and hadn't paid close attention.

Wen Mingyue's menses had previously been regular, but after Xie Zigui left, they became irregular.

Counting the days, it probably wasn't the case. However, Wen Mingyue's parents had passed away early, and there was no one to tell her these things, no one to analyze it for her.

She had previously heard people say that there were rare pregnant women whose menses continued as usual, and they only discovered they were pregnant when the time came to give birth.

Wen Mingyue harbored this lingering fear, so having a doctor come take a look would be best.

If she were truly pregnant, Wen Mingyue was resolved not to keep it.

She did not want any entanglement with Xie Zigui, nor could she afford to have any.

Hearing Wen Mingyue's concerns, Peilan was also unsure; such matters were truly unpredictable.

They said that under heavy rewards, brave men would step forward. If enough silver was thrown, naturally someone would come.

This didn't require any extraordinary skill, as long as they simply knew how to take a pulse.

The doctor did not arrive until nightfall, presumably wishing not to be seen. Even after taking the silver, his face remained cold.

He wore a dead-serious expression while taking the pulse, as if everyone owed him a debt.

Moreover, the pulse-taking lasted a very long time, so long that Peilan's heart grew frantic. "Doctor, how is my young mistress?"

The doctor did not speak, continuing to take the pulse with his eyes closed. The atmosphere in the room grew increasingly heavy. After a long while, the doctor finally spoke, "From my examination of the pulse, the young lady shows no signs of joy; it is quite ordinary."

His words were very blunt.

"But my young mistress has vomited several times," Peilan said, disregarding the disdain in his tone as she hurriedly pressed him.

"Judging by your accent, you are not locals?" The doctor asked an unrelated question.

Wen Mingyue was the first to react, explaining that they had just arrived.

That being the case, the doctor's explanation fell into place: Pingcheng's terrain and climate were different from ordinary places, and upon arriving, one was bound to need a few days to adjust, in plain terms, homesickness and acclimatization issues.

However, the symptoms of acclimatization varied from person to person; some reacted as soon as they arrived, while others needed a day or two.

Wen Mingyue's case was still considered mild; some suffered severe bouts of vomiting and diarrhea, enduring terrible hardship.

The doctor gave his explanation and then wrote a prescription for Wen Mingyue to take.

In truth, there was no great cure; it was simply a matter of resting for a few days.

For these few days, she was not to eat anything raw or cold, and not to get angry.

"Can the young mistress rest easy now?" Peilan poured warm water and held it out before her.

Right now, the matter wasn't particularly grave; it was just the terrifying suspense of not knowing the outcome that filled one with dread.

Look at Xie Zigui: every other word was about how his heart was set on Wen Mingyue, yet at this hour he was nowhere to be seen. He couldn't help with the slightest thing, but all the trouble came from him.

Wen Mingyue murmured an assent. "It was just my own wild imagination."

Now that she had regained her rationality, she found herself utterly ridiculous. The notion of menstruating throughout pregnancy was likely something made up in popular romances, yet she had applied it to herself.

Making herself scared over nothing.

Peilan had initially been amused by Wen Mingyue's words, but after laughing twice, her tears uncontrollably spilled over. "Young mistress, this servant hates the master."

Now that she had calmed down, the lingering fear grew stronger. It was fine if Wen Mingyue was currently unharmed, but if a major crisis had truly occurred, Xie Zigui would be a guest of honor serving as the prefect in Pingcheng, while her own young mistress suffered in bitter isolation with no one to care for her.

She had previously thought the heavens were good to her young mistress: although the master and mistress had passed away early, Wen Mingyue's fate wasn't too bitter because Xie Zigui was left behind to accompany her. But now it seemed all her young mistress's hardships were caused by Xie Zigui.

If not for Xie Zigui, Wen Mingyue's life might have been infinitely smooth and prosperous.

Becoming an official's wife was not necessarily a must-have for Wen Mingyue.

She managed the Wen family on her own, with food and clothing in abundance; there was no need to fight for those empty titles.

Wen Mingyue raised a hand to gently wipe away Peilan's tears. "You silly girl, life is never completely smooth-sailing. Knowing when to stop in time is already a great achievement."

In a few days, they would leave Pingcheng, and with Xie Zigui, bridges would be bridges and roads would be roads. The difficult days right now would eventually pass.

"With this tearful look, how can I feel at ease when you get married in the future?" Seeing the ever-increasing tears she was wiping from Peilan's face, Wen Mingyue sighed helplessly.

"This servant won't get married at all. This servant will just stay and guard the young mistress; don't even think about chasing me away," Peilan replied, sniffling.

Wen Mingyue nodded helplessly. "If you don't marry, you don't marry. You can stay with me and become an old maid."

Either way, she could afford to support this little girl.

Hearing Wen Mingyue's promise, Peilan finally broke through her tears into a smile.

They say that when people fall ill, it is when they yearn most for their family; if they have no family, they long for their hometown.

At this moment, anyway, Peilan particularly wanted to return to Zhaozhou City.

To return to the familiar place where they belonged.

Even though being sick was unpleasant, Peilan had things on her mind and had to keep track of the medicine; it seemed as though the day passed in a flash.

The next day, Peilan calculated the time, news from Zhaozhou City should have arrived by now. She waited and hoped, from morning till nightfall, yet still no messenger appeared.

Peilan's heart inevitably sank.

She had personally found someone to send the letter out, so there shouldn't have been a slip-up.

Could it be that it was still too late? Had something happened to the Wen family?

Wen Mingyue had taken her medicine for a day and felt much better. She held a ledger in her hands, but lacked the heart to flip through it. "Let's wait a bit longer. Perhaps it will arrive tomorrow."

She had to give them time to prepare.

Just as they were speaking, Xie Zigui hurried in, a thick smile still hanging on his face as he carried a food box. "Mingyue, look what I brought you!"

Hearing him enter, Peilan immediately put on a cold face.

Wen Mingyue remained seated, merely placing the ledger in her hand to the side.

Xie Zigui pulled up a stool on his own and sat down beside Wen Mingyue, carefully opening the food box. Inside was a plate of lychees. "I only gave that fool two of these, and brought the rest all to you."

Lychees were difficult to transport; let alone coming to Pingcheng, even people in the capital rarely ate them.

It was true that the Wen family had silver, but making it possible to transport lychees all the way from the south was something only the imperial court could accomplish; merchants certainly didn't have that kind of capability.

This item was indeed a rarity, rarer even than gold.

Yet, not to mention Wen Mingyue, even Peilan couldn't be bothered to look at them. "The young mistress is unwell and cannot eat cold things."

chapters.title: A Concubine is a Concubine
chapters.content:
Hearing Peilan say this, Xie Zigui finally began to size up Wen Mingyue. "Why is your complexion looking so dreadful?"

Wen Mingyue cleared her throat, originally intending to reply, but Peilan spoke first. "Does the master not know? The young mistress has been vomiting terribly."

Weren't you still vomiting when he left?

Yet after just a single day, he had already forgotten?

Peilan was bottling up her anger, and finally found an opportunity to vent it.

Xie Zigui's face turned alternately red and white from being told off. "It's been two days and she's just been left looking like this? How are you servants tending to her? Why haven't you hurried to invite a doctor over?"

When Xie Zigui finished speaking, Peilan let out a cold "humph" and stood rigidly to the side, refusing to move.

Xie Zigui frowned slightly. "Look at this girl, she's been spoiled rotten by you. If she goes to the capital, she can't be lacking in manners like this. I don't mind it myself, but if outsiders were to see, they'd make a mockery of both you and me."

"Peilan has indeed been somewhat exhausted serving me these past two days. Whose work is it if not done?" Wen Mingyue originally intended to brush it off with a few perfunctory words, but since Peilan had already brought it up, Wen Mingyue naturally had to take over.

Xie Zigui didn't argue further with Wen Mingyue; instead, he raised a hand and instructed his subordinates to go fetch a doctor.

Only, he looked at the lychees with worry. "These things don't keep; I'm afraid they'll spoil by tomorrow."

With that, he looked up at Wen Mingyue.

Wen Mingyue sighed silently. "Send them to that young lady of the Marquis's estate. I lack this blessing."

Xie Zigui took Wen Mingyue's hand. "You and I, husband and wife, think alike. You truly possess the demeanor of a primary wife; we shall bestow them upon her."

He spun the food box around, winked at his subordinates, and as he handed it over, leaned close to whisper a few instructions in someone's ear.

With a moment's thought, Wen Mingyue knew: if he called someone obedient, it was simply because he knew how to coax them.

Giving instructions like that must mean he was going over to tell her how much she loved them, and how much trouble he had gone through to find them for her.

Wen Mingyue suddenly grew curious: if Xie Zigui ever found out that Wen Jiaoshu actually understood everything, would he be so ashamed and enraged that he wouldn't dare face people on the spot?

Her thoughts churned a thousand times, but she had no intention of speaking.

Xie Zigui, on the other hand, was quite excited, chattering on about many rare and curious things. As he rambled on, seeing that Wen Mingyue looked drowsy and wasn't listening at all, he felt awkward himself and coughed a few times after finishing.

"Since you're not feeling well, and I'm planning to perform the ancestral sacrifices tomorrow, I suppose I won't take you. When there's another opportunity next time, I'll take you along." Having said this, Xie Zigui even reached out to smooth down the fine hair at Wen Mingyue's temples, an angle that radiated the utmost deep affection.

"Your father, he..." Hadn't he already climbed up to high and mighty branches? Was he going to worship the ancestors by himself?

At the mention of his father, Xie Zigui's gaze was filled with bitter hatred. "He abandoned his wife and son; naturally, he wouldn't dare appear before the ancestors. The lintel of the Xie family must rest upon my shoulders to uphold."

He, the grand Top Scholar Xie, was the only one in the clan who could stand tall!

Wherever he appeared, that father of his wouldn't even dare show his face.

Tomorrow, the ancestral hall would open, and his status as Top Scholar should be supreme.

Wen Mingyue nodded. "Then is the Marquis's young lady going?"

The original hatred vanished instantly at these words; he flinched and didn't dare meet Wen Mingyue's eyes. "Since she has come, if she wants to go join in the lively atmosphere, she can go."

At such a reply, Wen Mingyue could only offer a cold laugh.

Anyone who did business knew that if the master of a house was hosting a banquet, invitations needed to be sent out in advance to show importance. If you were invited just a day prior, it meant they had been hesitating all along whether to invite you or not, in plain terms, you were dispensable. If you were invited on the very day itself, it meant they had never had any intention of calling you; even if you went, you were just there to make up numbers.

These past two days, Xie Zigui hadn't even mentioned it once, which showed that from the very beginning he had never intended to let Wen Mingyue go. Regardless of whether the Marquis's young lady came or not.

Calling each other husband and wife with every breath, yet anyone who couldn't be acknowledged publicly was merely a concubine.

"You, you're good at everything, except for being far too discerning." Xie Zigui shook his head helplessly. Seeing right through everything would only exhaust oneself. "You know my difficult position; why must you make things hard for me?"

Wouldn't it be better if appearances were kept up? Why did she have to lay everything out in the open and make a fool of him?

"Make things hard for you? Then why did you have to bring it up?" If he had been straightforward and honest, without playing those little tricks, without using her health as an excuse, how could things have ended up like this?

He only knew how to point fingers at others; why couldn't he reflect on what he himself had done?

Xie Zigui tapped the tip of Wen Mingyue's nose. "With your sharp tongue, in this lifetime, who besides me would ever dare want you?"

Not giving her husband an ounce of face, always striving to win, where was there any gentleness of a woman?

The husband as heaven; she must have truly studied the Precepts for Women for nothing.

"Didn't you already know what kind of person I was? If you weren't willing, why bother proposing marriage back then?" Father Wen had only this single twig on his family tree, and had never intended for her to spend her life serving a husband and raising children anyway.

What was the use of fighting over men? What Wen Mingyue wanted to fight for was a man's livelihood.

It wasn't as if Wen Mingyue had begged Xie Zigui to come.

You said you'd marry, so you married; you said I'd be the wife, so I was the wife; you said I'd be a concubine, so I'm a concubine. Clearly, you toyed with others like fools, so why are you now blaming all the faults on someone else?

"Fine, fine, fine. I shouldn't argue with you. Everything you say is right, alright?" Xie Zigui raised his hand, interrupting what Wen Mingyue wanted to say next like a plea for mercy.

When a person was blocked like that, their breath simply couldn't smooth itself out.

Right at that moment, the person previously sent out to invite the doctor returned.

Since Xie Zigui was inviting a doctor for Wen Mingyue, he certainly couldn't use the name of the great Scholar Xie, which meant that the cold shoulder Wen Mingyue received would also reflect on Xie Zigui.

Hearing this, Xie Zigui rubbed his brow with some distress. "It was my oversight."

That also explained why Peilan had been speaking to him with such barbed hostility.

"Tomorrow, tomorrow I will arrange for you to move elsewhere." Right now, even an inn was better than this place.

Peilan stood nearby holding a pair of scissors, feigning the trimming of the candle wick. Hearing this, the anger in her heart flared up again. "Does the master finally have his official salary now? Our young mistress has delicate skin and tender flesh; her accommodations must be comfortable."

If they were going to live in an inn, it had to be the finest rooms.

Though they didn't bring many people, those people all needed rooms too.

For the Wen family, such a tiny bit of silver naturally counted for nothing.

Xie Zigui didn't spend sparingly on ordinary days either, and had never worried about silver, which was why he thought of this solution. Now that Peilan had pierced through it, his face instantly dropped.

So what if you're a Top Scholar? Where did the silver for your trip to the capital for the examinations come from? Where did the silver for your ancestral sacrifices come from?

Wasn't it all paid for by these officials?

And yet he was still spending Wen family silver, opening and closing his mouth to demote the young mistress to a concubine, and on top of that, he had started learning how to point fingers and lose his temper at the young mistress?

Even if one raised a dog, it wouldn't turn around to bite its master.

Peilan could endure it as long as Wen Mingyue wasn't sick, but the moment Wen Mingyue fell ill, Peilan no longer cared about the bigger picture; she only knew that if she didn't speak her mind, she'd be driven mad with rage.

"Peilan!" Wen Mingyue lightly reprimanded.

Meeting Wen Mingyue's gaze, Xie Zigui's expression finally softened.

chapters.title: Who Is Fooling Whom?
chapters.content:
"You really need to teach this girl a proper lesson." Even so, he still muttered this under his breath.

He muttered it as if he could regain his lost face by simply saying the words.

You can never wake a person who is pretending to be asleep. He knew how terribly he had failed her, yet he chose to wrap himself in lies, managing to fool even himself.

"Should I find a place myself, or will you arrange it?" Wen Mingyue should have been angry, and perhaps she even blamed her parents for having taught her to be too reasonable.

The angrier she got, the calmer she became.

"Naturally, I will arrange it. You don't need to trouble your idle mind with this." Xie Zigui immediately tried to win some favor.

Wen Mingyue couldn't help raising an eyebrow. "You have your ancestral worship tomorrow, which is bound to be tedious. When will you return? When will you settle me in?" Or did he plan to just casually find someone and toss her off somewhere to be rid of her?

He was going to perform ancestral rites with his future wife, while leaving his former wife aside and letting the servants deal with her?

Whether it was finding a place or moving, he wasn't going to be involved at all?

Some things couldn't be solved with just a big talk; they required genuine, concrete actions.

Clearly, Xie Zigui had not thought that far ahead.

Xie Zigui gave a helpless shake of his head. "You, oh you. What am I to do with you?"

Wanting to handle everything in advance just made him look like a clown putting on a show.

Wen Mingyue did not reply. In the past, she had possessed confidence, but now she had misjudged the person sleeping right beside her, which was why she had ended up isolated and stranded away from home. How could she dare call herself smart?

"I'll have someone fetch some medicine for you to drink first. Once I free up my hands, I'll come and settle you in." This time, Xie Zigui was genuinely setting his mind to it.

He would surely return late tomorrow night, exhausted and unable to accomplish anything in a rush.

Wen Mingyue was obviously displeased. He certainly couldn't just leave everything to the servants like he had when she first arrived.

Wen Mingyue had been vomiting for two days now. Although her complexion looked poor, she still had spirit when she spoke, so he figured it couldn't be anything major; it certainly wouldn't hurt to wait another day or two.

She wasn't even a concubine yet, and she couldn't even see a doctor; once she truly became a concubine, there was no telling how she would be tormented.

If she trusted Xie Zigui, her days of suffering were likely yet to come.

"It's getting late. You should go back." Wen Mingyue did not want to argue any further. What was the point? Arguing would only end up making her angry at herself.

Xie Zigui thought for a moment and finally nodded. "Alright. I'll come over a bit later tomorrow. Get some good rest, sleeping more is good for your health."

When some people fell sick, simply sleeping could cure them.

Wen Mingyue turned her head away. As the esteemed head of the Wen family, was she now reduced to sleeping and waiting to die?

Seeing Xie Zigui stand up, Peilan briskly went to open the door. "This servant will see the master out."

"Just take good care of your young mistress; there's no need for all these empty, superficial gestures." Xie Zigui waved his hand repeatedly. There was no need for him to bicker with a maid, but this girl's mouth had been thoroughly obnoxious today.

Peilan curtsied to Wen Mingyue, completely ignoring him, and walked out first.

Xie Zigui let out a helpless sigh. "Fine, fine. Who asked me to spoil you? If your maid doesn't know her manners, then so be it."

His tone was clearly different from before.

In the past, he was the son-in-law of the Wen family, but now, Wen Mingyue had become a wife of the Xie family.

In that single instant, only eight characters crossed Wen Mingyue's mind: A poor man suddenly rich, a petty person showing off.

She had thought that an educated scholar like him would be different from the rest, but it turned out he was just as vulgar as any other.

After walking for a bit, Peilan returned in a huff.

"My lady didn't see it, but those two were out there in broad daylight, practically making a bed on the spot." Peilan had gone out because she had arranged for a doctor to come, and she didn't want them to cross paths. In case Xie Zigui still had a tiny shred of conscience left unbitten by dogs, he might feel a trace of pity for Wen Mingyue, so she had gone out early to tell the guards to keep a sharp lookout.

To her surprise, she ran into the young lady of the Marquis's estate waiting outside.

The moment she saw Xie Zigui, she called him "elder brother" with such an affectionate tone, offering a plate of leftover lychees as if it had utterly moved that young lady to tears.

Even knowing she was putting on an act, acting like that was truly nauseating.

A concubine-born daughter, a match made in heaven for a little ungrateful wolf.

Hearing Peilan ramble on, Wen Mingyue couldn't help but chuckle. "You, where on earth did you learn all these tricks?"

"This servant is a crude person anyway, and what I do best is scolding people." Before, that concubine-born woman was just pure murmuring without any real curses, especially among servants, whether legitimate or concubine-born, there weren't that many rigid rules.

But right now, only those few words could truly describe that young lady from the Marquis's estate.

"This servant is just worried. Do you think that concubine-born wretch can really accomplish anything major?" Looking at her, she didn't seem like someone who possessed deep concealment. If it were about fighting for favor within a household, she certainly had the means; but when it came to the outside world, Peilan had no confidence based on what she saw.

Wen Mingyue sighed softly. "I'm not gambling on how formidable she is; I'm gambling that Xie Zigui's reach in my Zhaozhou City isn't that long yet."

After all, Zhaozhou City was the deep root of the Wen family, with connections everywhere from top to bottom. It might be fine to send someone to the yamen to alter the marriage contract, but for anything more outrageous, people might not necessarily grant him that face.

In other words, it wouldn't be that easy for Xie Zigui to clear the crucial obstacles.

"Alright, for now we can only take it one step at a time." They were trapped in Pingcheng, and without outside help, news would reach them slowly.

Right now, they had no choice but to tear open a gap.

The ancestors of the Xie family probably did possess some real capabilities.

On the day of the ancestral worship, the sky was clear and vast, and at noon, auspicious clouds even appeared on the horizon.

Wen Mingyue sat in the courtyard, muttering to herself, "Does heaven sometimes turn a blind eye?"

Why else would it grant the Xie family such immense face?

Peilan walked over holding an umbrella. "My lady, don't let the sun make you dizzy."

Wen Mingyue slowly pulled back her gaze. Although she hadn't gone to the ancestral worship, she could easily imagine how immensely smug Xie Zigui must feel with the appearance of these auspicious clouds.

"If we cannot get people out, we must find a way to get goods out." Wen Mingyue removed the token of the family head from her hand. "Tell him: As long as the green hills remain, there's no need to worry about firewood."

Her own people must preserve their strength above all else.

No matter what, they could not choose mutual destruction.

"My lady." Peilan had originally been very anxious, but seeing Wen Mingyue remain calm all this time, she had finally managed to ease her mind. Yet Wen Mingyue's sudden words made her heart leap into her throat again.

What did this mean? Was Zhaozhou City about to undergo a drastic change?

Wen Mingyue looked steadily at Peilan. "If possible, you should do the same."

Stay alive first.

Wen Mingyue looked up at the auspicious clouds, and the ominous premonition in her heart grew stronger by the minute.

Judging by the time, the people from the Wen family should have arrived by now, which meant something must have gone wrong.

The people she could openly use were no longer usable; she had to find someone whose existence even Xie Zigui knew nothing about.

This was the method left behind by the Wen ancestors, the ultimate method for a comeback.

Peilan vigorously wiped her eyes. "This servant will certainly accomplish it."

No matter what method it took, she would get the message out.

After Peilan left, Wen Mingyue returned to her room, took out a fake token she had prepared earlier, put it on her finger, and continuously twisted it.
